content: Conjugated estrogens can have their effects altered by changes in intestinal flora, which is relevant only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure in such cases is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Pentobarbital reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenytoin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. If conjugated estrogens are used for contraception, there is a potential risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is essential. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Prednisone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through mechanisms involving OAT3 inhibition. In vitro studies show significant OAT3 inhibition, necessitating close monitoring for adverse effects and potential dosage adjustments for OAT3 substrates. Primidone reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quercetin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Quinupristin/dalfopristin alters intestinal flora, reducing the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Quinupristin/dalfopristin also increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ranolazine increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Roxithromycin alters intestinal flora, reducing the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Simvastatin increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sirolimus increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of somapacitan by decreasing serum IGF-1 response. Patients may require higher somapacitan dosages. Refer to the drug monograph for starting dose recommendations. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Stiripentol affects CYP1A2 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer, potentially altering the effects of conjugated estrogens. Close monitoring and therapy modification may be required. Streptomycin alters intestinal flora, reducing the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole, and sulfisoxazole reduce the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Tacrolimus increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels or effects of tazemetostat by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. Teicoplanin and temocillin alter intestinal flora, reducing the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Tenapanor reduces the levels of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the intestinal uptake transporter OATP2B1. Caution and monitoring are advised. Teniposide increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Tesamorelin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering metabolism. Monitor for reduced efficacy. Tetracycline, tigecycline, and tobramycin alter intestinal flora, reducing the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Tolvaptan increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Trazodone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Trimethoprim alters intestinal flora, reducing the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels or effects of ubrogepant by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustment is recommended when used with moderate or weak CYP3A4 inducers. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by increasing OAT3 substrate exposure. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust substrate doses as needed. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels or effects of valproic acid by increasing its elimination, potentially leading to increased seizure frequency. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Vancomycin alters intestinal flora, reducing the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Conjugated estrogens may interact with tricyclic antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, amoxapine, clomipramine, desipramine, dosulepin, doxepin, imipramine, lofepramine, maprotiline, nortriptyline) by reducing their effects while increasing plasma concentrations and adverse effects. The interaction mechanism is unspecified, and the clinical significance is unclear. Conjugated estrogens decrease the levels of ascorbic acid, cyanocobalamin, exemestane, folic acid, L-methylfolate, magnesium salts (e.g., chloride, citrate, hydroxide, oxide, sulfate), and valproic acid by altering metabolism or increasing elimination. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Conjugated estrogens decrease the effects of metyrapone and mycophenolate by unknown mechanisms. The clinical significance is unclear. Phytoestrogens and pleurisy root may reduce the effects of conjugated estrogens through pharmacodynamic antagonism or unspecified mechanisms. These interactions are theoretical, and their clinical significance is unknown. Natural progesterone and conjugated estrogens may interact through pharmacodynamic mechanisms.
